item.description:
ONI 1.5, the slide film and contact sheet update.

  • The whole roll, once measured: after Prepare the Roll, every frame shows together, numbered by its place on the film.
  • Contact sheets: select a few frames, or press the orange key for the whole roll, and they lie together on one sheet.
  • Export a contact sheet: the export panel exports the selection as one sheet, with a preview; the orange EXP. CONTACT SHEET key opens it.
  • Slide films: Prepare the Roll balances a slide roll on a white or grey you click, its colour alone; without a click, the slides keep the camera's 5500 K.
  • Contact sheets on black: every contact sheet, slides included, lies on black, numbered in orange; the logo shows under a full row of five.
  • The whole scan in Prepare: every scan is shown and measured uncropped.
  • RESET SCAN keeps your crop: everything goes back to rest but the framing and the conversion.
  • Trash from the editor: the next frame of the roll opens in its place.
  • Select all beside a photo: the folder's photos show together; a click on one shows it alone again.
  • No more flicker on Windows: clicking outside the window and back no longer blanks it for an instant.
  • Large 16-bit TIFFs: a 16-bit TIFF of 45 Mpx and more opens, in the editor and in Prepare the Roll.
  • A scan that cannot be read says why: Prepare the Roll no longer waits on it.
  • Nikon High Efficiency RAW: a click converts a folder’s HE and HE* NEF files to lossless DNGs through Adobe DNG Converter, which ONI downloads and installs when it is missing.
  • One RAW decoder, the same colours everywhere: a RAW opens in the same colours on Mac and Windows. The Mac's per-camera matching to the former Apple decoder is gone; photos you already edited keep their look through their Source Balance gains until their roll is measured again.
  • Windows updates itself: from 1.5.3 on, the app finds the next versions and installs them when you ask, as on the Mac; an older copy is updated once by hand.
  • Compare on a contact sheet: Compare Before/After splits the whole sheet, each frame shown on its own before.
  • Every frame follows: on frames shown together, switching to the Scanner face or choosing another proof redraws every frame, not the open one alone.
  • Crop and De-dust wait for one frame: a crop, a measuring window or a dust spot belongs to one photo, so they are greyed while frames show together.
  • Take a frame out: after Select All, a ⌘-click (Ctrl-click on Windows) in the column takes a frame out of the group, and a second puts it back.
  • The folded Library shows whole: slid over the canvas, it no longer cuts its fields and stars at its edge.
  • A quieter look: the raised and sunken surfaces are half as deep, the histogram lies on the scanner screen's black, and the canvas is square where it meets the panel or a folded column.
